svg.title: In development: getting ready for Linux 7.3 on Proxmox VE 9
svg.desc: A Proxmox server drawn in a flat, sticker-style illustration stands on a wooded hill at sunset. Its chassis plate reads Proxmox VE API, the part that stays the same. Parts snap into its sockets one at a time, each a roadmap item: a version screen reading the installed kernel; a blue 7.0 kernel cartridge that is ejected and swapped for an orange 7.3 one, the opt-in kernel; a wrench on a side hook for deploy_pve_vm; a nested PVE sled that slides into a drive bay, a second cluster for Datacenter Manager tests; and a power cable that plugs in and lights the LEDs, for live runs of the deploy tools. Stickers on the left check off each part. A taped-on heads-up note cycles through what could change: ZFS disk utilization readings, the kernel.org-based build, and new boot-log lines. A wavy sticker marquee along the bottom reads In development, Try on kernel 7.3, Same API underneath, Parts may swap, Nested node incoming, One API, new parts.

g.text: ZFS disks may show higher %util on 7.3.
Real load, or new counting? Still checking.
7.3 is built from kernel.org, not Ubuntu,
so a patch or two may be missing.
New boot-log lines (W^X, TDX) are expected.
Proxmox VE 9 has an opt-in Linux 7.3 kernel. We're fitting the parts now.
